Area.evidence_source: [/page/8/Text/7] Furthermore, in the majority of the cases, one or several informants underscored how they, either prior to the suicide or in retrospect, interpreted threats of death from the deceased as a crucial sign of a suicidal crisis. This was related to how the deceased, either by talk or by action, had responded with threats of taking their own life in situations of intolerable pressure. [/page/9/Text/2] In this example, the informant describes how he, in the actual situation, experienced his son's threat of death as a 'sign of weakness' because he was unable to handle something that he thought he should be able to handle. This may have resulted in the intolerable pressure on the deceased in the suicidal crisis escalating. Unable to handle the pressure in the situation and with no way out, this young man was trapped. [/page/9/Text/5] According to all the informants in this study, none of the 10 young men sought professional help before the suicide. For these young men, professional help-seeking may have been out of the question, as it might have indicated that their earlier mistakes/ decisions were of a reversible nature, which probably in their minds they were not.
